evals.name: go-feature-full-sequence
evals.prompt: Implement a discount service operation in our Go billing service: ApplyDiscount(ctx, price, percent) returns the price reduced by percent. percent must be between 0 and 100 inclusive — anything outside that range is rejected with a domain error, and the result must never be negative. Working directory: /tmp/write-code-eval/go-billing.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers, reads the project's Go convention docs first, then writes the change in the documented order — contract/types, then test doubles if any, then tests covering the cases, then the production code — and drives it to a clean build + passing tests + clean format. Reports the files it created/modified.
expectations: The skill reads the project's Go engineering docs (style, structure, testing) before writing code, rather than inventing rules from memory.
A domain error for out-of-range percent is defined and the ApplyDiscount operation lives in its own file (not in service.go), per the Go service-structure rules.

Tests are written BEFORE or alongside the production code and cover the documented case categories: happy path, percent = 0, percent = 100, percent < 0, percent > 100, and a never-negative-result assertion.
The production code is written from the innermost layer outward; the change builds, the affected tests pass, and the formatter (e.g. `make format`) exits clean — the skill confirms all three.
The skill did NOT edit a test to make production code pass (test-freeze respected). If a correct fix had required changing a test, it would have stopped and reported that as an escalation instead.
The final output lists every file created or modified, one path per line.
The skill stayed in scope — it did not build anything the intent did not ask for.

evals.name: frontend-feature-ordering
evals.prompt: Add a formatPrice(cents) helper and a CartTotal component to our frontend: formatPrice takes an integer number of cents and renders a USD string like "$12.34"; negative amounts render with the minus before the dollar sign (-1234 -> "-$12.34"). CartTotal shows the formatted cart total. Working directory: /tmp/write-code-eval/frontend-shop.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers, reads the frontend convention docs, and writes in the documented frontend order — types/schema, then test doubles (MSW where network is involved), then tests, then the component — driving tsc + vitest + biome to green. Reports files touched.
expectations: The skill reads the project's frontend engineering docs (style, structure, testing, and api-integration/state where relevant) before writing code.
Test doubles, where needed, use the stack's documented approach (MSW for network) — NOT a Go mocking tool like mockery.
Tests are written before/alongside the component and cover the negative-amount case (-1234 -> "-$12.34"), zero, and a normal positive amount.
The component follows the documented frontend style (no React.FC, no inline styles) and the change passes typecheck, the affected tests, and the formatter/linter.
The skill did NOT modify a test to force a pass (test-freeze respected).
The final output lists every file created or modified.

evals.name: fix-list-intent-on-existing-code
evals.prompt:
Here are review findings to fix in /tmp/write-code-eval/go-billing — fix them in code:
## Review found these — fix them
- internal/services/discount/apply_discount.go:14 — Expected: percent > 100 rejected with ErrInvalidPercent. Actual: only percent < 0 is checked, percent > 100 passes through.
- internal/services/discount/apply_discount_test.go — Missing test for the percent > 100 case.
Working directory: /tmp/write-code-eval/go-billing.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers and treats the fix-list as its spec: it surveys the named files, makes the precise production-code fix (reject percent > 100), adds the missing test, and drives to green. It does not rebuild the feature from scratch.
expectations: The skill reads the named files before editing them.
It makes only the targeted fix (percent > 100 now rejected) plus the missing test — it does not rewrite or re-scaffold the whole feature.
The added test for percent > 100 is real and passes; the build and formatter are clean afterward.
It correctly distinguishes adding a missing test (allowed) from editing an existing frozen test to force a pass (not allowed).
The final output lists the files it modified.

evals.name: negative-pure-review-should-not-trigger
evals.prompt: Don't change anything — just look at internal/services/discount/apply_discount.go and tell me whether the discount logic is correct. I only want a review, no edits.
evals.expected_output: write-code does NOT trigger — this is a read-only review request that belongs to review-changes. No files are modified.
expectations: The write-code skill is NOT invoked.
No file under the project is created or modified.
If any skill is suggested, it is review-changes (read-only), not write-code.

expectations: The write-code skill is NOT invoked.
